nodes.title: Total cohomology invariance over absolutely integrally closed valuations
nodes.statement: Let V → W be a faithfully flat homomorphism of valuation domains whose fraction fields are algebraically closed. Fix a prime ℓ invertible in V and a commutative coefficient ring Λ killed by ℓⁿ, n > 0. For any qcqs V-scheme X and E ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ), put X_W = X ×_V W and g: X_W → X. The canonical cohomology pullback β_g(E): RΓ(X,E) → RΓ(X_W,g*E), obtained from E → Rg*g*E and the direct-image/global-sections composition isomorphism, is an isomorphism in D⁺(Λ). Consequently H^q(X,E) → H^q(X_W,g*E) is an isomorphism for every integer q. There is no finite-type or constructibility assumption in this bounded-below form.
hypotheses: V and W are valuation domains, with no rank, completeness, discreteness or microbial hypothesis.
φ: V → W is faithfully flat; equivalently in this valuation setting it is injective and local, and Spec W → Spec V is surjective.
ℓ is prime, n > 0, Λ is a commutative ring with ℓⁿΛ = 0, and ℓ is a unit of V (therefore also of W).
X is qcqs over Spec V; E belongs to D⁺(X_ét, Λ).
Both fraction fields are algebraically closed; since valuation domains are normal, these are absolutely integrally closed valuation rings.
proofSteps: Use Stacks Lemma 15.14.5 (0DCQ) and the inherited algebraically-closed-fraction-field-strictly-henselian node to identify the algebraically closed fraction-field hypothesis with the absolutely integrally closed condition used by Hansen–Scholze.

For affine X of finite presentation, use the scheme supplier’s finite ℓ-cohomological-dimension bound (Hansen–Scholze Lemma 3.5, d+1) to reduce to constructible sheaves, with coefficient reduction to Z/ℓⁿ and compatibility with forgetting Λ-modules. Approximation reduces the valuation rank to finite rank.

Induct on that rank using E → Rj*j*E and its cone supported over a proper closed subset of Spec V. The requested H1:valuation-nearby-cycles generic-extension theorem is Hansen–Scholze Theorem 4.1: on separated finitely presented schemes over an absolutely integrally closed valuation, extension by Rj* identifies constructible generic coefficients with universally locally acyclic coefficients. Its formation commutes with flat absolutely integrally closed valuation changes (Corollary 4.2(ii)). After reducing constructible Z/ℓⁿ-sheaves by their ℓ-power filtration to F_ℓ-coefficients, bounded constructible coefficients are perfect, so this ULA theorem applies. On this term compute cohomology on the generic fibre; the closed-support term uses induction on the quotient valuation. Field-extension invariance is the requested scheme theorem, Stacks 0F0B.

Hansen–Scholze Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.2 use the pro-étale Rj* on perfect-constructible coefficients. Transfer the bounded-below torsion case through ν*: D⁺(X_ét,Λ) → D⁺(X_proét,Λ). The SF.2 supplier must retain the unit identification E ≅ Rν*ν*E and functorial pullback, Rj* and global-sections comparisons (Bhatt–Scholze Corollary 5.1.6, Proposition 5.2.6, Lemmas 5.4.1 and 5.4.3). The generic inclusion is affine, so Lemma 5.4.3’s qcqs hypothesis holds even when it is not open. Carry the adjunction-unit triangle and canonical cohomology map through these comparisons; no unrestricted unbounded étale/pro-étale identification is inferred. Use the typed subscript correction recorded in E-H1-valuation-exports-1.

The final paragraph of Hansen–Scholze Corollary 4.5 treats D⁺ without a finite-type condition: reduce in a fixed cohomological degree to a constructible sheaf on an affine chart, descend the chart and sheaf along an affine inverse system of finite-type schemes, and use étale cohomology continuity. Import AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2/etale-cohomology-continuity. Extend to qcqs X by descent on affine charts with quasi-compact intersections; use bounded-below truncation, not an unbounded-totalization interchange.

Every reduction must carry the canonical adjunction-unit map β, not just an abstract isomorphism of groups. The SF.2 request fixes these coefficient, descent and composition identifications. The public proof establishes the result, while these typed supplier inputs remain open planning requests.

nodes.title: Total cohomology invariance with separably closed fraction fields
nodes.statement: In the notation and coefficient range of total-cohomology-valuation-invariance, suppose only that Frac V and Frac W are separably closed. For any qcqs V-scheme X and E ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ), the same canonical map β_g(E) is an isomorphism. In positive characteristic this is obtained by passage to the purely inseparable perfect closures of the fraction fields and their valuation rings, followed by descent through universal homeomorphisms. No claim that a separably closed field is already algebraically closed is made.
hypotheses: V and W are valuation domains, with no rank, completeness, discreteness or microbial hypothesis.
φ: V → W is faithfully flat; equivalently in this valuation setting it is injective and local, and Spec W → Spec V is surjective.
ℓ is prime, n > 0, Λ is a commutative ring with ℓⁿΛ = 0, and ℓ is a unit of V (therefore also of W).
X is qcqs over Spec V; E belongs to D⁺(X_ét, Λ).
Frac V and Frac W are separably closed, with imperfect positive-characteristic fields admitted.
proofSteps: In characteristic zero the separably closed fraction fields are algebraically closed, so apply total-cohomology-valuation-invariance directly.

In characteristic p > 0, let K^perf and L^perf be the perfect closures of K = Frac V and L = Frac W. They are algebraically closed because the original fields are separably closed. The unique purely inseparable extensions of the valuations give V^perf ⊂ K^perf and W^perf ⊂ L^perf, equivalently the integral closures of V and W. This is the algebraic valuation input used in the inherited radicial-invariance-of-nearby-cycles node, not a new definition of nearby cycles.

The maps Spec V^perf → Spec V and Spec W^perf → Spec W are universal homeomorphisms. They preserve the spectrum order and the closed point. The extension V^perf → W^perf is injective and local, hence faithfully flat by the inherited surjective-valuation-base-change criterion.

Apply total-cohomology-valuation-invariance to this bottom valuation map. The scheme supplier’s topological invariance (Stacks §59.45) makes both vertical cohomology maps isomorphisms, including after base change to X. Naturality and composition of β make the square commute; hence the original β_g(E) is an isomorphism.

Alternatively apply torsion-sheaf-valuation-adjunction-descent to cohomology sheaves after coefficient forgetful functors. The exact unit is an isomorphism on sheaves and hence on bounded-below complexes, using finite truncations in each degree and the left exact derived functor. This route uses Huber 4.2.7 directly and does not require algebraic closure.

sources.match: Supplies the algebraically closed fraction-field case after the radicial reduction; it does not itself state the separably closed extension.
A universal homeomorphism identifies étale sites and cohomology; this transports the canonical map through the two perfection maps.

Directly supplies the separably closed torsion-sheaf statement. Bounded-below ℓ-power coefficients on qcqs schemes follow by truncation and canonical adjunction descent; the existing radicial proof is retained as an independent route.

In positive characteristic use an imperfect separably closed field with a valuation: the proof must include its radicial perfect closure, rather than asserting an IsAlgClosed instance from IsSepClosed.

nodes.title: Closed-support cohomology invariance under valuation base change
nodes.statement: Let V → W, Λ, X and E satisfy total-cohomology-separably-closed-valuation-invariance. Let Z be a closed subset of X whose open complement U is quasi-compact (therefore qcqs). Write Z_W = g⁻¹(Z). The canonical pullback with closed supports β_g,Z(E): RΓ_Z(X,E) → RΓ_Z_W(X_W,g*E) is an isomorphism in D⁺(Λ), and H^q_Z(X,E) → H^q_Z_W(X_W,g*E) is an isomorphism in the same degree q for every integer q. This map is the closed-support functoriality map in the natural localization triangle. It commutes with forgetting supports, restriction to U and the connecting morphisms. Closed support is imported from EDC.0; it is neither cohomology of Z nor compactly supported cohomology of X.
hypotheses: V and W are valuation domains, with no rank, completeness, discreteness or microbial hypothesis.
φ: V → W is faithfully flat; equivalently in this valuation setting it is injective and local, and Spec W → Spec V is surjective.
ℓ is prime, n > 0, Λ is a commutative ring with ℓⁿΛ = 0, and ℓ is a unit of V (therefore also of W).
X is qcqs over Spec V; E belongs to D⁺(X_ét, Λ).
Both fraction fields are separably closed.
Z ⊆ X is closed and X∖Z is quasi-compact; no finite-boundary hypothesis is substituted for this explicit condition.
proofSteps: Import EDC.0/cohomology-with-supports and the scheme supplier’s morphism of localization triangles for the pair (X,U) and its base change: RΓ_Z(X,E) → RΓ(X,E) → RΓ(U,E|U) → RΓ_Z(X,E)[1]. Stacks §59.79 constructs this triangle from injective resolutions.
Apply total-cohomology-separably-closed-valuation-invariance to X and U. The pullback of U is precisely X_W∖Z_W, and the two ordinary-cohomology vertical maps are isomorphisms.

The long exact sequences of the two localization triangles and the five lemma show that the supported vertical map is an isomorphism. Retain the same degree on the two supported terms: the shift belongs to the connecting morphism, not to the invariance isomorphism.
Naturality of the supplier’s localization triangle proves compatibility with restriction and forgetting supports. No arbitrary Ri^! base-change isomorphism is inferred at sheaf level.

sources.match: Provides the two ordinary-cohomology invariance maps in the localization argument, after the separably closed reduction.

sources.locator: §59.79 (09XP), the global localization triangle before Lemma 59.79.1; Lemma 59.79.3 (0A45); unpaginated HTML
sources.match: Closed-support cohomology is the fibre of restriction to the open complement. Applying total invariance to both ordinary terms gives the stated consequence.

acceptance: Z = X reduces to total cohomology invariance; Z = ∅ yields the zero object.

For a rank-one valuation V with closed point s and nonzero Λ supported by E = i*Λ, H⁰_s(Spec V,E) = Λ. It stays Λ after faithfully flat valuation extension; this distinguishes supported cohomology from deleting the special fibre.

For a microbial valuation, take Z = f⁻¹(V(p_V)); the complement is X_η, and the support triangle agrees with the inherited special-locus-support-triangle. In rank two this Z need not be the closed fibre.
The claim is in degree q on both sides. The separate proper comparison H^q_Z(X,E) = H^{q−1}(X_s,RΦE) uses the inherited proper-nearby-cycle-cohomology theorem and must keep its shift.

nodes.title: Coherence of total, proper nearby and tube invariance maps
nodes.statement: Let V → W be faithfully flat valuation rings with separably closed fraction fields K,L; let ℓ be invertible in V, ℓⁿΛ = 0, and f: X → Spec V proper. For X_W, write g_η: (X_W)_η′ → X_η and g_s: (X_W)_s′ → X_s. Let j,j′ be the generic-fibre maps and i,i′ the closed-fibre maps. Put RΨF = i*Rj*F. For F ∈ D⁺((X_η)_ét,Λ), let α_X(F): RΓ(X_η,F) → RΓ(X_s,RΨF) be the canonical proper comparison, and inv_φ(F) the inherited nearby invariance map (cohomology pullback along g_s followed by cohomology of the nearby base-change transformation). Then α_X(F) followed by inv_φ(F) equals β_gη(F) followed by α_X_W(g_η*F). Both α maps and β_gη are isomorphisms, so this identifies inv_φ with geometric-generic cohomology pullback. The comparison can also be computed through β_g(Rj*F) followed by RΓ of g*Rj*F → Rj′*g_η*F; total invariance alone must not omit that exchange transformation. If V,W are microbial with valuation topologies, the ring map is continuous, and the completions and tubes satisfy the imported formal-adic-compatibility hypotheses, the same equality transports through κ_X and κ_X_W to the canonical tube pullback square.
hypotheses: Proper f; both fraction fields separably closed; faithful flatness preserves closed and generic points.
The prime-power coefficient assumptions of the new total-cohomology theorem are retained. The inherited proper-nearby comparison itself permits a larger torsion range.

Formal/tube transport additionally requires the actual microbial, continuous, type-(S) setting of the inherited formal-adic comparison. Purely scheme-theoretic invariance supplies no adic continuity assumption.
proofSteps: Use the inherited proper-nearby-cycle-cohomology theorem to identify α_X with the composite RΓ(X_η,F) ≅ RΓ(X,Rj*F) → RΓ(X_s,i*Rj*F), and similarly over W. These are maps defined by restriction, not chosen cohomology isomorphisms.

Expand inv_φ by the inherited invariance-comparison-map and expand β by the SF.2 adjunction-unit formula. The naturality of the unit and the two commutative fibre squares give equality of the composites. Coherent direct-image composition and its base-change mates are a precisely requested SF.2 input. The nearby exchange transformation is imported from H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-base-change-map.

The generic valuation rings are fields, so the separably closed total-invariance theorem gives β_gη an isomorphism. The two α isomorphisms then identify inv_φ with β_gη. This proper argument does not require replacing the full nearby-cycle sheaf map by a claim of arbitrary sheafwise cohomological base change.

For the alternative calculation through X, use total-cohomology-separably-closed-valuation-invariance at Rj*F, followed by the cohomology of the generic-fibre exchange map. Its composition with direct-image/global-sections is the same β_gη. No finite-type assumption is imposed on the generic inclusion at higher valuation rank.

For the formal transport, import formal-adic-compatibility and completion-comparison-base-change-naturality unchanged. Conjugate the equality by their κ maps. Construction of the adic site, completion and pseudo-adic supports stays with the cited owner nodes.

acceptance: For V = W and φ = id, inv_φ and β_gη are identities and the square reduces to α_X = α_X.
For X = P¹_V, rank one or higher, the induced degree-zero map fixes 1; degree two preserves the first Chern class of O(1), giving Λ(−1) with the specified Tate-twist normalization.
For rank-two microbial V and W, use the actual closed-point tube in Spa(K,V). Continuity and the plus ring V are retained under κ; rank-one completion cannot silently replace the tube.
With η = s (V a field), j and i are identity maps and the square is ordinary geometric-field cohomology pullback.

Residue-characteristic torsion is not asserted by these new invariance nodes. The larger torsion scope of proper-nearby-cycle-cohomology does not enlarge the prime-to-residue total-invariance theorem.

nodes.title: Sheaf local cohomology along a constructible valuation boundary
nodes.statement: Let A,A′,q,X,p be as above, and let F be an abelian torsion sheaf on X_ét with torsion orders prime to the residue characteristics occurring on X′. For a closed constructible Z ⊆ S such that Z′ = q⁻¹Z is a proper subset of S′, set T = f⁻¹Z and T′ = p⁻¹T, with open complements r and r′. For every n ≥ 0 the canonical map p*Rⁿr_*r*F → Rⁿr′_*r′*p*F is an isomorphism. Equivalently the canonical sheaf-local support map p*𝓗ⁿ_T(X,F) → 𝓗ⁿ_T′(X′,p*F) is an isomorphism. These are sheaves on X′, not global support groups. The derived local-support exchange is an isomorphism on F[0].
hypotheses: A and A′ are valuation domains with separably closed fraction fields; arbitrary rank, including fields, is admitted.
q: S′ = Spec A′ → S = Spec A is any scheme morphism; X is any S-scheme and p: X′ = X ×_S S′ → X is the actual projection.
F is a torsion abelian sheaf prime to char(X′); a common annihilator is not required.
Z is closed and constructible in the base spectrum; q⁻¹Z ≠ S′. No surjectivity, dominance, finite-type, properness or qcqs assumption is made.
proofSteps: Use the actual complement restriction and local-support triangle from EDC.0; in degrees zero and one its local cohomology is the kernel and cokernel of F → r_*r*F, and in degree n ≥ 2 it is Rⁿ⁻¹r_*r*F.

At a geometric point over Z′, let η and η′ be the closed points of S∖Z and S′∖Z′. Closed constructibility makes these complements quasi-compact open intervals of the chain of primes. The map q takes η′ to η. These points can be non-generic in rank greater than one.

Apply the full Cartesian nearby-base-change theorem Huber Proposition 4.2.4, p. 243 and proof pp. 246–249, to the corresponding quadruples (X,S,η,s) and (X′,S′,η′,s′). Its no-finite-type, non-dominant range is explicitly requested from the nearby-cycle owner; the narrower existing node is not silently used.

The canonical nearby exchange agrees stalkwise with the restriction exchange for r; outside T′ that exchange is the identity. The support triangle then gives the local-cohomology comparison in every degree, with its actual canonical map.

sources.locator: Corollary 4.2.6(i) and proof, pp. 243–244; Proposition 4.2.4, p. 243 and proof pp. 246–249
sources.match: This is the sheaf-local comparison under arbitrary valuation-base change with a proper pulled-back base boundary. It is distinct from the previously planned global closed-support consequence.

acceptance: For Z = ∅ both local-support complexes are zero and the open-restriction comparison is the identity.
For identity q the comparison is the canonical identity on local cohomology.
For a rank-two base choose a compact open complement with more than one point; the proof uses its closed point and must not replace it by the generic point.
A localization map of valuation rings is allowed when the pulled-back boundary remains proper; no surjectivity condition is inserted.

nodes.title: Vanishing when a valuation boundary collapses to one base point
nodes.statement: With A,A′,q,X,p,F as in local-cohomology-valuation-base-change, take any proper closed constructible Z′ ⊊ S′, and let η′ be the closed point of S′∖Z′. Assume q(z′) = q(η′) for every z′ ∈ Z′. If T′ = f′⁻¹Z′, then 𝓗ⁿ_T′(X′,p*F) = 0 for every n ≥ 0. Equivalently the local-support complex on p*F[0] is zero, or the canonical p*F → Rr′_*r′*p*F is an isomorphism. Global support cohomology also vanishes by the support spectral sequence.
hypotheses: A and A′ are valuation domains with separably closed fraction fields; arbitrary rank, including fields, is admitted.
q: S′ = Spec A′ → S = Spec A is any scheme morphism; X is any S-scheme and p: X′ = X ×_S S′ → X is the actual projection.
F has prime-to-char(X′) torsion, with no common exponent required.
Z′ is a proper closed constructible subset of S′, not necessarily the pullback of a subset of S.
η′ is the closed point of its open complement, and all points of Z′ have the same q-image as η′.
proofSteps: At a geometric point over z′ ∈ Z′ put s = q(z′) = q(η′). The target quadruple has η = s; this equality is essential.

For this degenerate quadruple nearby restriction in degree zero is the original stalk, and all positive-degree nearby cohomology vanishes. Apply the full Cartesian nearby comparison of Huber 4.2.4 to the source quadruple.
The restriction map p*F → Rr′_*r′*p*F is a stalkwise isomorphism. The local-support triangle gives zero in every local-cohomology degree.
Use the requested first-quadrant local-to-global support spectral sequence to obtain vanishing of global Hⁿ_T′, rather than identifying local-cohomology sheaves with global groups.

sources.match: The collapse hypothesis permits non-surjective maps and gives local vanishing from the η=s case of nearby cycles.

acceptance: A rank-one valuation A′ with separably closed fraction field over a separably closed base field A satisfies the collapse condition for its closed point. The result applies to sheaves pulled back from an A-scheme.
Z′ = ∅ gives the zero support complex.
For identity q and a nonempty proper boundary, the collapse hypothesis fails; no vanishing is asserted for an arbitrary special-fibre sheaf.

nodes.title: Total cohomology of arbitrary torsion sheaves under surjective valuation change
nodes.statement: Let A,A′ have separably closed fraction fields and q:Spec A′→Spec A be surjective. For any A-scheme X and abelian torsion sheaf F on X_ét whose torsion is prime to char(X), the canonical cohomology pullback Hⁿ(X,F) → Hⁿ(X ×_A A′,p*F) is an isomorphism for every n ≥ 0. Equivalently β_p(F[0]) is an isomorphism in D⁺(ℤ). There is no uniform exponent, ℓ-primary, finite-type, qcqs or constructibility requirement.
hypotheses: A and A′ are valuation domains with separably closed fraction fields; arbitrary rank, including fields, is admitted.
q is surjective on spectra, equivalently its ring map is injective and local or faithfully flat.
X is any S-scheme. F is an abelian torsion sheaf on X_ét prime to char(X); it need not be constructible or killed by one integer.
proofSteps: Reduce in a fixed cohomological degree to finite-rank valuation bases by the scheme supplier’s affine-limit and torsion-coefficient continuity; use affine étale charts and descent for arbitrary X. This is not descent of a finitely presented constructible pair and is recorded separately in the supplier request.

For dimension-zero target base, the collapsed-boundary vanishing theorem removes the nongeneric strata of the source finite-rank valuation. Compare the remaining generic fibre by prime-to-characteristic invariance over separably closed fields, Stacks 0F0B (with its qcqs chart hypothesis, then sheaf descent).

For positive finite rank choose a nonempty proper closed base interval. Its complement and the quotient valuation defining that interval both have smaller dimension. Apply local-cohomology-valuation-base-change, the support spectral sequence and induction to supported cohomology; apply induction to the open complement.

Compare the canonical localization long exact sequences to obtain the isomorphism on total cohomology. The arrows throughout are induced by p and its adjunction unit, so the conclusion identifies β_p rather than an unspecified group isomorphism.

sources.match: The original sheaf theorem has a broader coefficient and scheme range than the retained Hansen–Scholze bounded-below specialization.

acceptance: Identity q induces the identity on Hⁿ.
Rank-zero valuations recover prime-to-characteristic separably closed field invariance.
An unbounded direct sum of sheaves killed by varying invertible integers is admitted as a torsion sheaf; it is not an arbitrary unbounded derived complex.
For a non-surjective generic localization, a nonzero special-fibre skyscraper loses its global sections; surjectivity cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: Adjunction descent for torsion étale sheaves over valuations
nodes.statement: Under torsion-sheaf-total-cohomology-valuation-invariance, the canonical adjunction F → p_*p*F is an isomorphism and Rⁿp_*p*F = 0 for all n > 0. Thus the specific derived adjunction unit F[0] → Rp_*p*F[0] is an isomorphism, natural in F and compatible with composition of surjective valuation changes. The statement is about the pulled-back sheaf p*F; it does not make p an equivalence on all sheaves on X′.
hypotheses: A and A′ are valuation domains with separably closed fraction fields; arbitrary rank, including fields, is admitted.
q is surjective on spectra, equivalently its ring map is injective and local or faithfully flat.
X is any S-scheme. F is an abelian torsion sheaf on X_ét prime to char(X); it need not be constructible or killed by one integer.
proofSteps: Apply the preceding global theorem to every affine étale U→X, with U′=U×_A A′ and F|U. Étale charts form a basis even when X is not qcqs.
The section computations give F(U) ≅ (p_*p*F)(U); the positive-degree computations kill all derived direct-image sheaves.
Identify the degree-zero map with the adjunction unit. Naturality and composition are the general supplier’s unit/coherence laws, not an additional choice of isomorphisms.
Use exact inverse image, bounded-below truncations and derived-unit naturality to recover the retained D⁺ specialization; do not claim an unrestricted unbounded derived statement.

sources.match: Records both the degree-zero sheaf identity and the positive-degree vanishing, which mere global group invariance would not state.

acceptance: On each étale U, H⁰(U,F) is carried by the actual adjunction unit.
For the identity valuation map the unit is the identity and all positive direct images vanish.
On a separably closed base field the theorem agrees with the sheaf form of Stacks 0F0B.
No assertion that every sheaf on X′ descends, and no arbitrary Rⁿp_*G vanishing, is made.

nodes.title: Finite-rank descent of finitely presented valuation data
nodes.statement: Let A be a valuation domain with separably closed fraction field, f:X→Spec A finitely presented, B noetherian killed by m>0 prime to char(X), F a constructible B-module on X_ét, and Z a closed constructible subset of Spec A. There exist a valuation subring A₀⊆A with separably closed fraction field and finite Krull dimension, an injective local inclusion A₀→A (hence q:Spec A→Spec A₀ surjective), a finitely presented f₀:X₀→Spec A₀, a closed constructible Z₀, and a constructible B-module F₀ on X₀_ét such that X≅X₀×_A₀ A over A, Z=q⁻¹Z₀ and F≅p*F₀ under this identification. The model can be chosen with m prime to char(X₀).
hypotheses: A is a valuation domain with separably closed fraction field; S = Spec A.
B is a noetherian commutative ring killed by some m > 0 prime to char(X), and F is a constructible étale B-module on X.
Constructibility is affine-local finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes, with finite-type locally constant B-modules on the strata; X need not be noetherian.
f is finitely presented, including quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness; Z is closed constructible.
proofSteps: Use affine-limit descent of finitely presented schemes, their gluing, constructible subsets and constructible sheaves. All presentations, covers, strata, étale trivializations and their finite-module gluing descend after enlargement to a common finite stage. This is requested from SF.2 with the existing L2 continuity node.

For the finite collection of ring coefficients needed by the descent, choose a finitely generated subfield k of Frac A containing them, and its relative separable closure K₀ inside Frac A. Put A₀=A∩K₀. Its valuation is the restriction of the original valuation, the inclusion is local, and K₀ is separably closed.

Finite rank of the restricted valuation follows from the bound for a valuation on a finitely generated field over its prime field; algebraic extension does not add rational rank. The value-group rank is bounded by rational rank. This exact algebraic finite-rank capture input is requested from the existing AdicSpaces valuation-foundation stage, rather than assumed to be in the library.

Include the finitely many coefficients making m invertible on the affine pieces of X among the descended data. Faithful flatness of A₀→A and finite presentation preserve the stated model and coefficient identifications.
The resulting finite spectrum makes Z₀ finite. Its pullback and sheaf identification retain the canonical projection maps needed by local-support base change and total invariance.

sources.locator: Proof of Corollary 4.2.8, part (2), p. 245; proof of Corollary 4.2.9, part (2), p. 246
sources.match: Makes the finite-rank model used by both finiteness proofs an explicit key input. It is distinct from the inherited reduced finite-presentation model over a fixed topologically noetherian valuation base.

acceptance: For finite-rank A one may take A₀=A and the identity model.
The coefficient sheaf and Z must descend together with X; descending only defining equations is insufficient.
In rank greater than one no discrete or rank-one approximation is asserted.
The conclusion is an actual Cartesian model over A; the corrected orientation of the p. 246 displayed base change is retained.

nodes.title: Constructibility along a finite valuation boundary
nodes.statement: Let A,B,F satisfy the finiteness conventions, f:X→S be locally of finite type, and Z⊆S closed constructible. Put T=f⁻¹Z and j:X∖T→X. If either f is locally of finite presentation or Z has finitely many points, then Rⁿj_*j*F and, equivalently, 𝓗ⁿ_T(X,F) are constructible B-module sheaves for every n≥0. The finite boundary is Z in the base spectrum. Neither properness nor quasi-compactness of X is required.
hypotheses: A is a valuation domain with separably closed fraction field; S = Spec A.
B is a noetherian commutative ring killed by some m > 0 prime to char(X), and F is a constructible étale B-module on X.
Constructibility is affine-local finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes, with finite-type locally constant B-modules on the strata; X need not be noetherian.
f is locally of finite type, and Z is closed constructible.
Either f is locally of finite presentation, or the underlying point set Z is finite. These are alternatives, not simultaneous assumptions.
proofSteps: In the finite-Z branch, each singleton in Z is constructible and locally closed. On the open complement j*F is already constructible; on the fibre over s∈Z, identify the restriction of Rⁿj_*j*F with nearby cohomology for η the closed point of S∖Z and s.

Apply the imported constructibility-of-nearby-cycles theorem (Huber 4.2.5, p. 243 and proof pp. 251–256). A finite partition of the base boundary then combines the fibrewise constructibility with that on the open complement.

For the locally-finite-presentation branch work on affine charts, where the morphism is finitely presented. Apply finite-rank-descent-of-valuation-data to X,F,Z together. The descended boundary Z₀ in the finite-rank model is finite.

Apply the finite-Z branch to the descended model. Local-cohomology-valuation-base-change identifies the actual Rⁿj_*j*F with its constructible pullback. Handle Z=S separately, where j has empty source and local support is F[0]; this avoids using the proper-boundary theorem outside its hypotheses.
The localization triangle gives the equivalent constructibility of the local-cohomology sheaves using noetherian-coefficient closure under kernels, cokernels and extensions.

sources.locator: Corollary 4.2.8 and proof, p. 245; Proposition 4.2.5, p. 243 and proof pp. 251–256
sources.match: Supplies both alternatives exactly. Finiteness refers to the closed constructible subset of Spec A, not a quasi-finite exceptional locus of X or a compactification boundary.

acceptance: Z=∅ yields R⁰j_*j*F=F and higher terms zero; all local-support sheaves vanish.
Z=S yields Rⁿj_*j*F=0 and local support F in degree zero.
If A has finite rank then every Z is finite, so the locally-finite-type branch applies without finite presentation.
For infinite-rank A with finite Z, locally finite type suffices. For an infinite Z, retain local finite presentation; no finite-type-only claim is made.

nodes.title: Finite generation of ordinary constructible cohomology over valuations
nodes.statement: Let A,B,F satisfy the finiteness conventions and let f:X→Spec A be of finite type. If either f is of finite presentation or dim A<∞, then Hⁿ(X_ét,F) is a finitely generated B-module for every n≥0. This is ordinary global cohomology, with no properness or separatedness hypothesis in the finite-dimensional branch. No uniform vanishing range or finite cardinality is claimed.
hypotheses: A is a valuation domain with separably closed fraction field; S = Spec A.
B is a noetherian commutative ring killed by some m > 0 prime to char(X), and F is a constructible étale B-module on X.
Constructibility is affine-local finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes, with finite-type locally constant B-modules on the strata; X need not be noetherian.
f is of finite type globally, hence quasi-compact and locally of finite type.
Either f is finitely presented (including quasi-separatedness), or A has finite Krull dimension.
proofSteps: For finite-dimensional A induct on dim A. Dimension zero is the requested prime-to-characteristic constructible-cohomology finiteness theorem for finite-type schemes over a separably closed field (Huber cites SGA 4½, Th. finitude 1.10). Its exact general coefficient and nonseparated range is recorded as a scheme-supplier request.

For positive dimension the generic point η is open constructible. Take U=X_η and T=X∖U. The finite base boundary S∖{η} permits constructibility-along-finite-valuation-boundary for the sheaves 𝓗ⁿ_T(X,F).

Apply induction to T over the smaller-rank quotient valuation base. In the first-quadrant support spectral sequence Hᵖ(T,𝓗ᑫ_T(X,F)|T) ⇒ Hᵖ⁺ᑫ_T(X,F), all terms contributing to a fixed degree are finitely generated. Noetherianity of B preserves finite generation through subquotients and extensions.
The generic fibre has finite-type constructible cohomology over a separably closed field. The localization long exact sequence for (X,U) then gives finite generation of Hⁿ(X,F).

For finitely presented X over arbitrary-rank A, descend X,F to the finite-rank model and apply the preceding branch there. Torsion-sheaf-total-cohomology-valuation-invariance carries global cohomology along the surjective spectrum map; the B-linear comparison is the same canonical map after coefficient forgetful functors.

sources.match: This is the ordinary global finiteness theorem missing from the earlier proper/nearby finiteness exports. It records finite presentation or finite base dimension, rather than guessing a finite-boundary condition on X.

acceptance: A separably closed field A reduces the theorem to the scheme supplier’s classical finiteness result.
For finite-rank A, any finite-type X in the stated coefficient range is admitted, including nonproper X.
For infinite-rank A, retain finite presentation; no finite-type-only theorem is asserted.
Finitely generated over a noetherian torsion ring B can be an infinite set when B is infinite. The conclusion must remain Module.Finite, not Finite.
For X=P¹_A and constant B, H⁰ is B and H² is B(−1); this checks ordinary global cohomology and the standard twist, not compact support.

requests.need: On the EDC.0 bounded-below derived étale carrier of qcqs schemes, provide exact inverse image, Rg*, their adjunction, RΓ and the coherent isomorphism RΓ_X Rg* ≅ RΓ_Y. Fix β_g = RΓ_X(unit) followed by that isomorphism, with naturality, identity and composition. Supply the bounded-below pullback map of the imported EDC.0 localization triangles, with natural connecting arrows; topological invariance under universal homeomorphisms (Stacks 04DY); geometric-field cohomology invariance (0F0B); and the cohomological-dimension, filtered-constructible/coefficient and affine-descent inputs of Hansen–Scholze Lemma 3.5 and Corollary 4.5. The existing Brauer, coherent-duality and equivariant-support SF.2 nodes were inspected and do not supply these exact scheme-étale inputs. Also supply the general scheme ULA predicate on perfect-constructible coefficients: after every scheme base change and for every geometric x over s and geometric generization t of s, the canonical Milnor-fibre comparison E_x → RΓ(X_(x) ×_S_(s) t,E) is an isomorphism (Hansen–Scholze Theorem 4.4(iii), p. 22). General ULA belongs to this scheme-cohomology supplier; its valuation-specific generic-extension theorem remains with H1:valuation-nearby-cycles. Use the exact L2 higher-cohomology-continuity node already cited, rather than a second continuity carrier. Include the same bounded-below étale/pro-étale realization already requested by AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L1, together with its functorial comparisons: ν* is fully faithful with E ≅ Rν*ν*E, commutes with inverse image, and for a qcqs f:Y→X has ν_X* Rf_ét,* E ≅ Rf_proét,* ν_Y* E (Bhatt–Scholze Corollary 5.1.6, Proposition 5.2.6 and Lemmas 5.4.1, 5.4.3, author-copy pp. 35, 37, 39). Preserve adjunction units, localization triangles and RΓ under the comparisons. The generic localization j is affine, so its Rj* meets the qcqs hypothesis. Proposition 5.3.2 is an unbounded left-completed statement, not permission to identify unrestricted unbounded classical étale complexes with pro-étale complexes. Use the corrected functor subscripts in E-H1-valuation-exports-1. This extends the existing SF.2 request, not a new owner or category. Extend these functors and unit/localization maps to arbitrary schemes on the bounded-below carrier, by affine étale chart descent. Supply sheaf local cohomology i_*Ri! separately from global RΓ_T, the canonical pullback exchange, its restriction compatibility, and the first-quadrant local-to-global support spectral sequence. Supply constructible B-module sheaves over general, possibly nonnoetherian schemes using finite constructible locally closed stratifications on each quasi-compact open; include exact-category closure, pullback, coefficient forgetful compatibility, and descent of such sheaves, strata and finitely presented schemes along affine inverse limits. Provide the arbitrary torsion-sheaf, finite-rank-base approximation used by Huber 4.2.7 independently of descent of finitely presented constructible data. Provide finite generation of Hⁿ(X,F) for a finite-type scheme over a separably closed field, B noetherian killed by m>0 prime to the field characteristic, F constructible, every n≥0; no properness or separatedness restriction. Huber 4.2.9 p. 246 cites SGA 4½, Th. finitude 1.10, whose text has not been read in this run. Stacks 0F0B supplies field-extension invariance on qcqs charts, but not this general finiteness theorem.

Extend the existing arbitrary-valuation nearby-cycle plan by the generic-extension result actually used in Hansen–Scholze Corollary 4.5: for a separated finitely presented X over an absolutely integrally closed valuation V, with j: X_K → X, Rj* takes perfect-constructible torsion generic coefficients to ULA objects and is inverse to generic restriction on the ULA subcategory (Theorem 4.1, pp. 19–22); retain flat AIC valuation-base compatibility (Corollary 4.2(ii), p. 19). The existing i*Rj* constructibility and valuative nearby-base-change nodes do not imply this Rj*/ULA result on the total scheme. Import the general scheme ULA definition from its supplier instead of reusing diamond ULA or creating another coefficient category. State the theorem first on the source’s pro-étale realization of the perfect-constructible carrier, then provide its bounded-below torsion étale form through the SF.2 comparisons; retain both the canonical generic adjunction unit and the flat-valuation exchange map in this transfer. Also extend the existing valuative-base-change-for-nearby-cycles node to the full Huber Proposition 4.2.4 statement, p. 243 and proof pp. 246–249: Cartesian morphisms of quadruples, any X, and torsion abelian F prime to the characteristic exponent at the target special point; neither locally finite type nor dominance is assumed. The existing restricted node is retained as a specialization, not duplicated in valuation-exports. This full form is required by both local-support results. Use the already owned constructibility-of-nearby-cycles node for Proposition 4.2.5.

For a valuation domain A with separably closed fraction field K and any finite subset of A, provide a separably closed subfield K₀⊆K containing that subset, such that A₀=A∩K₀ is a valuation domain of finite Krull dimension and A₀→A is injective and local. Choose a finitely generated prime-field subfield carrying the finite data and take its relative separable closure in K; justify the finite-rank bound for the restricted valuation and its preservation under algebraic extension. Retain the actual subring and local inclusion, not a rank-one replacement or a discretely valued model. This is the algebraic input of the owned finite-rank descent lemma, whose scheme/sheaf descent belongs to SF.2. Supply also strict henselianity of valuation localizations whose fraction fields are separably closed, and separably closed fraction fields of their valuation-domain quotients, as needed to form the quadruples and run rank induction. The existing algebraically-closed-fraction-field-strictly-henselian import covers the algebraically closed specialization only.

coverage.note: All targets are represented by the eleven retained H0 imports and eleven nodes here. The original finite-boundary, finite-dimension and full torsion-sheaf statements have exact hypotheses and locators. The stage is planned rather than closed because its proof suppliers and assembled planet selection remain explicit requests/refinements.
remaining: Supply the three exact cross-owner requests: scheme functors/constructibility/continuity/finiteness, the full Cartesian nearby-base-change theorem and generic Rj*/ULA theorem, and finite-rank algebraic capture.
Refine the finite-rank descent and arbitrary torsion-sheaf approximation proofs after those interfaces are supplied; do not substitute the inherited reduced-model lemma.
Retain the inherited formal-completion naturality and generic compactification/finiteness prerequisites from H0; this pass does not discharge them.
Reconcile H0 and follow-up planet nominations through the proposed three-part split or select at most six planets in the assembled unsplit star.

gaps.title: Exact scheme and nearby proof suppliers
gaps.detail: The source statements and proofs have been read, but current supplier nodes do not include all required maps, general constructibility/descent, arbitrary torsion approximation or finite-type generic-field finiteness. In particular the existing nearby-base-change node has locally-finite-type and dominant hypotheses absent from the full Huber 4.2.4 statement. The first two requests specify the missing generality and canonical maps. The SGA 4½ finiteness input is identified through Huber, not represented as independently source-read. The inherited H0 formal/adic and compactification gaps are not declared resolved.

gaps.title: Finite-rank capture and constructible descent
gaps.detail: Huber 4.2.8–4.2.9 assert finite-rank models with descended sheaf data. The key descent lemma is now a target, with algebraic finite-rank capture requested from the existing valuation foundation and finite-presentation/constructible-sheaf limit descent from SF.2. Neither the finite-rank subfield theorem nor the combined descent API was found at the current or pinned library. The actual Cartesian model and sheaf pullback must be constructed before this proof chain is closed.

restructure.detail: The stage combines six inherited H0 planets with four new nominations for scheme invariance and finite-boundary/global finiteness. An unsplit assembled star would exceed the six-planet limit.
restructure.proposal: Propose three assembled stars: scheme-invariance (the retained bounded-below invariance, new local-support and torsion-sheaf targets, and algebraic coherence; two planets: Valuation cohomology invariance and Valuation support invariance); finite-boundary-and-finiteness (finite-rank descent, constructibility and ordinary global finiteness; two planets: Finite-boundary constructibility and Constructible cohomology finiteness); nearby-and-tubes (all eleven H0 imports and formal transport, retaining its six existing planets). Keep current ids until a restructuring proposal is applied. Assembly must implement this split or select at most six planets in the unsplit star; these are nominations, not ten simultaneously drawn planets.

sourceIssues.locator: Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-étale topology for schemes: Lemma 5.4.3 and proof, author-hosted 72-page copy p. 39 (SHA-256 in sources); also published Astérisque 369 (2015), pp. 153–154, in the academic mirror listed in sourceVersions.
sourceIssues.printed: For f:Y→X and F on Y_ét, the displayed pushforward comparison labels the realization after f_ét,* by Y and the realization before f_proét,* by X. The first affine test object in the proof is placed over Y, and the final bounded-below input is placed over X.
sourceIssues.correction: The comparison is ν_X* Rf_ét,* F → Rf_proét,* ν_Y* F. The affine test object U and its finite-stage U_i belong over X; their inverse images under f belong over Y. The final derived input is F ∈ D⁺(Y_ét). Preserve f qcqs and F bounded below.
sourceIssues.reason: Direct image of F lives on X_ét and can only be realized by ν_X*. Realization before direct image must take F from Y_ét to Y_proét, hence uses ν_Y*. Likewise f⁻¹U_i is defined for test objects over X. The commutative topos square in Lemma 5.4.1 and the section calculation in the proof determine these corrections uniquely; no mathematical conclusion changes.
searched: Author-hosted paper and Scholze’s public pages, accessed 2026-10-08: the p. 39 display retains the reversed subscripts; no linked correction was found.
Published Astérisque 369 article through the public academic mirror: Lemma 5.4.3 pp. 153–154 retains the same subscript and test-object slips.

SMF article listing and web searches for Bhatt Scholze 5.4.3 typo and pro-étale errata, 2026-10-08: no correction found. The arXiv record was checked as a version lead, not read as an additional full text.

sourceIssues.locator: Corollary 4.2.9 proof, p. 246, support spectral sequence and part (2) Cartesian-model display, first edition 1996.
sourceIssues.printed: The local-support spectral-sequence coefficient is labelled by the boundary T instead of F. The later model display repeats X as its own factor and puts the base rings on the wrong sides of the fibre product.
sourceIssues.correction: Use 𝓗ᑫ_T(X,F) as the coefficient sheaf. With A′ the smaller finite-rank valuation ring and X′ its model, the intended identification is X≅X′×_A′ A, with projection p:X→X′ and F≅p*F′.
sourceIssues.reason: T is a subset, not a coefficient sheaf, and the next conclusion concerns Hⁿ_T(X,F). The surrounding definitions place X′ over A′ and X over A; the surjective spectrum map goes from Spec A to Spec A′. This determines the Cartesian-model orientation and agrees with the p. 245 descent construction.

sourceIssues.printed: The final inverse/direct-image adjunction expression in that reduction is applied to the generic-fibre sheaf D, although its map p_s lies between the special fibres.
